headline: Highest risk is medium: plano can exfiltrate PDF-derived content over broad egress, while pdf.js is browser-based and local-only, creating leakage and cascade risks but no direct prompt-injection channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. pdf.js is a document-processing browser-based worker with PDF-file I/O only, while plano is an out-of-process AI gateway with API calls and config.yaml. Without a bridge like shared filesystem or clipboard, prompt injection between them is not evidenced.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected by a shared filesystem or copy-paste bridge, reassess upward.
IF plano begins ingesting raw PDF text from pdf.js as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Disable any manual copy-paste of PDF text into plano prompts.
Add provenance labels to any transferred text.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation between document text and instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js touches PDF documents locally and has no network egress, but plano has broad network egress and sends to an OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint. If PDF content or traces are forwarded into plano, sensitive document data can leave the local boundary in default use.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied into plano prompts or logs, leakage risk is present.
IF plano forwards document-derived text to its chat completions endpoint, leakage risk is present.
mitigations: Do not route PDF text into plano by default.
Redact sensitive fields before any transfer.
Use a local-only staging folder for pdf.js outputs.
Review plano logging and disable verbose request logging.
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering before API calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to files in some form, but the profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same directory or shared mutable resources. pdf.js supports multiple instances and plano does not support subprocesses; the main conflict is limited unless an operator co-locates their files.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, conflict risk increases.
IF plano and pdf.js modify the same config or output files concurrently, reassess upward.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes to shared files.
Use per-agent filenames.
Check for file-lock support before co-running.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce extracted document content that plano may consume through its chat-completions workflow. plano is a routing/gateway component, so if it treats pdf.js output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream decisions or generated outputs.
conditions: IF plano uses pdf.js output as authoritative input without validation, cascading error risk is present.
IF pdf.js extraction errors are not checked before plano acts on them, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require human review of extracted text.
Add checksum or citation checks on transferred content.
Keep pdf.js output read-only until verified.
Use a validation step before plano consumes any extraction.
requires-engineering: implement structured provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles. pdf.js is local document-processing with no egress, while plano is an AI gateway with API calls; the only compliance concern is operator-controlled transfer of document data into plano, which is not shown by default.
conditions: IF regulated document data is sent from pdf.js into plano's API path, compliance review is required.
IF retention policies differ for transferred document data, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated PDFs to plano.
Document the data flow before deployment.
Set retention limits on any transferred logs.
Confirm jurisdictional requirements for the API endpoint.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data.
